unit_routes.description: A string is the legacy routing edge. A rich route is a learner-facing material option for one unit: it explains the lecture-specific angle and coverage but does not impose an order.

id.description: Stable route identity. Required on every route written in data-contract v13; absent only on readable pre-v13 evidence until the recorded migration persists it.

format.description: What kind of artifact this is, which governs how it is used. 'exam' (past papers) and 'solutions' (worked model answers) are deliberately separate from 'exercise': a past paper is spent once under timed conditions, and model solutions are read as writing samples rather than solved.

angle.description: One line: what this material does for this lecture that the other options on it do not. Written for this lecture, never copied from the global source record.

angle_detail.description: The long form of the same judgment, shown on hover: what the reader gets, what it assumes, and where it departs from the taught deck. Optional only because the 2026-08 backfill is incremental; a newly authored route writes it.

depth.description: How deep this route goes. 'unassessed' means no contextual evaluation has been written yet, so the depth is genuinely unknown — it is not a judgment of shallowness and must never be inferred by an operator (CLAUDE.md §4).

scope.description: How this route relates to current exam scope. 'unevaluated' is distinct from 'optional': optional means assessed and judged skippable, unevaluated means the source is routed here but nobody has ever assessed it — visibility debt, made visible so it can be chosen or dismissed deliberately, and repaid on use rather than in bulk (WORKFLOWS §6a).

requires_assets.description: Files the activity itself needs before it can be done — a dataset it analyses, a code template it fills in. Distinct from the material being reachable: `_resource_available` answers 'can he open the worksheet', and this answers 'can he do what the worksheet asks'. Blatt 4 Aufgabe 3(b) needs International_Education_Costs.csv and aufgabe3.py from Moodle, neither registered here, and the session still reported the route ready (audit workbench/audits/synthetic-learner-2026-09-12, F06). An entry with no `material_uri` is by definition unregistered; the session keeps the route and names the parts that cannot be attempted, rather than dropping the runnable work or inventing a substitute dataset.

needed_for.description: Which part of the activity, in the sheet's own numbering.

obtain_from.description: Where the exact file comes from. Never a substitute.

exposes_solutions_for.description: Route ids whose activities this material answers — a verifiable claim about content, that opening this hands over the worked solutions to those tasks, never a judgment of quality. The session compiler refuses to put such a route in the same proposal as an evidence step it answers: explaining with the answer key and then asking for unaided transfer on that same task measures nothing (audit workbench/audits/synthetic-learner-2026-09-12, F03).
